title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 220: The Demise of the Mental Map
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 220 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Demise of the Mental Map: Spatial Cognition in the Digital Age

Paragraph 1. For thousands of years, humans travelled across lands and oceans without digital maps or satellites. To avoid getting lost, early travellers looked carefully at mountains, rivers, and stars to build mental maps inside their heads. Today, however, most people follow smartphone GPS voice directions. Instead of noticing landmarks like old bridges or tall trees, modern drivers just turn left or right when a phone tells them to.

Paragraph 2. Inside our brains, a small seahorse-shaped part called the hippocampus handles space and direction. In the early 2000s, scientist Dr. Eleanor Maguire studied the brains of London taxi drivers. To get their work license, taxi drivers spend three or four years learning twenty-five thousand city streets by memory. Maguire found that this memory centre was much bigger in London taxi drivers than in ordinary people, showing that active map-learning grows the brain.

Paragraph 3. When people follow turn-by-turn GPS apps, that important brain area goes completely quiet. Drivers develop 'tunnel vision' and stop watching buildings along the street. As a result, when a phone battery dies or loses signal, users often get lost even on streets they visit every single day. Doctors also worry that losing navigation skills may weaken the brain as people grow older.

Paragraph 4. Scientists now share simple tips to keep our sense of direction healthy. They suggest turning off GPS on familiar routes near home so the brain must remember turns and judge distances alone. Software makers are also designing smarter map apps that guide drivers with famous buildings, such as telling them to turn right after a big stone church.

q1.text: In the past, human travellers found their way without using satellite tools.

steps: Đoạn 1: Hàng nghìn năm trước con người đi lại không có bản đồ số hay vệ tinh.

q2.text: London taxi drivers earn much higher salaries than bus drivers.

steps: Đoạn 2: Chỉ nói tài xế taxi học 25.000 con phố, không so sánh thu nhập với tài xế xe buýt.

q3.text: GPS users always find their way home easily when their phone stops working.

steps: Đoạn 3: Khi điện thoại hết pin hoặc mất sóng, người dùng hay bị lạc ngay cả trên phố quen.

q4.text: Switching off GPS on roads you already know helps keep the brain active.

steps: Đoạn 4: Tắt GPS trên tuyến đường quen buộc não tự ghi nhớ và ước lượng khoảng cách.
Đoạn 4: "...turning off GPS on familiar routes near home..."
